calls.head: Bruisers against finesse
calls.body: On physicality, Florida sits 1st of 32, at the bruising end of the scale. Los Angeles is 27th, at the finesse end.
calls.call: Florida hits more than Los Angeles in the close stretches of the game.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: On hit score in close games (arena-adjusted, 100 is league average), Florida had 190 and Los Angeles 77. Coming in, Florida was at 144 and Los Angeles at 88.

calls.head: One power play bites, one doesn’t
calls.body: Florida ranks 8th of 32 for power play, toward the lethal end; Los Angeles ranks 27th, toward the harmless end.
calls.call: Florida’s power play creates more per 60 than Los Angeles’s.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: On power-play expected goals per 60, Florida had 7.6 per 60 and Los Angeles 4.7 per 60. Coming in, Florida was at 8.0 per 60 and Los Angeles at 7.1 per 60.

LAK.head: We had this close to even (58% for Los Angeles), and it went Florida’s way.

FLA.head: We had this close to even (42% for Florida), and Florida came through.

surprises.head: Florida was kept to the outside
surprises.body: Florida needed 23.6 unblocked shots per expected goal at 5-on-5, against its usual 16.2 and a league average of 15.9. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 20 games.

surprises.head: Florida brought the hits
surprises.body: Florida’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 190, against its usual 144 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 10 games.
